title: Tier 1: Framework Theories
description: The 10 neurally grounded, cross-domain frameworks. Every architectural effect must operate through one or more of these.
criteria: Mechanistic specificity — connects to neural implementation
Cross-domain generativity — predictions across multiple domains
Convergent multi-method support — fMRI, EEG, lesion, computational, behavioral evidence

predictive-processing.name: Predictive Processing
predictive-processing.core_mechanism: The brain continuously generates predictions about sensory input; mismatches (prediction errors) drive learning and attention allocation.
predictive-processing.key_principle: Efficient coding — familiar/expected stimuli processed more efficiently, freeing cognitive resources.

spatial-navigation.name: Spatial Navigation / Cognitive Mapping
spatial-navigation.core_mechanism: Hippocampal-entorhinal system constructs allocentric spatial representations; environmental legibility affects map quality and wayfinding success.
spatial-navigation.key_principle: Architectural legibility determines cognitive map fidelity; poor maps → wayfinding failure → stress.

dual-process-evaluation.name: Dual-Process Evaluation
dual-process-evaluation.core_mechanism: Two processing systems — System 1 (fast, automatic, affective) and System 2 (slow, deliberate, cognitive) — compete for behavioral control.
dual-process-evaluation.key_principle: Environmental features can bias which system dominates; high arousal/threat → System 1.

default-mode-dynamics.name: DMN/TPN Dynamics
default-mode-dynamics.core_mechanism: Default Mode Network (internal mentation) and Task-Positive Network (external attention) reciprocally inhibit; environmental demands modulate switching.
neural_substrates: DMN: medial prefrontal, posterior cingulate, angular gyrus
default-mode-dynamics.key_principle: Low-demand environments allow DMN engagement → restoration, creativity; high-demand → TPN dominance → fatigue.

neuromodulatory-systems.name: Neuromodulatory Systems
neuromodulatory-systems.core_mechanism: Dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine, and cortisol systems modulate arousal, reward, and stress; architectural features trigger these pathways.
neuromodulatory-systems.key_principle: Environmental novelty → dopamine; threat → cortisol/norepinephrine; comfort → serotonin/parasympathetic.

interoceptive-constructionist-affect.name: Interoceptive / Constructionist Affect
interoceptive-constructionist-affect.core_mechanism: The brain constructs emotions from interoceptive signals (body state) + environmental context; architecture affects body budget predictions.
interoceptive-constructionist-affect.key_principle: Environmental demands affect 'body budget' predictions; chronic allostatic load degrades health.

memory-systems.name: Memory Systems
memory-systems.core_mechanism: Episodic, semantic, and procedural memory systems encode environmental experiences; spatial context is central to episodic memory.
memory-systems.key_principle: Architectural distinctiveness creates memorable places; routine spaces blur together.

embodied-cognition.name: Embodied Cognition
embodied-cognition.core_mechanism: Cognition is grounded in sensorimotor experience; environmental affordances shape thought through action possibilities.
embodied-cognition.key_principle: Architectural affordances activate motor simulations; space is understood through potential action.

chronobiological-regulation.name: Chronobiological Regulation
chronobiological-regulation.core_mechanism: Circadian rhythms entrained by light; architectural light affects melatonin, cortisol, alertness, and sleep quality.
chronobiological-regulation.key_principle: Daylight exposure entrains circadian system; artificial light at wrong times disrupts rhythms.

multisensory-integration.name: Multisensory Integration
multisensory-integration.core_mechanism: The brain combines information across sensory modalities; congruence enhances processing, incongruence creates confusion.
multisensory-integration.key_principle: Multisensory congruence → fluency, comfort; incongruence → discomfort, effort.
